name: Empowering a Generation of Confident, Caring Teachers

content.title: Empowering a Generation of Confident, Caring Teachers
content.summary: IED EA's project equips tutors to mentor future educators, improving learning outcomes

media.caption: Tutors from Shanzu Teachers College pose with their certificates during the F4L closing ceremony in Mombasa, Kenya.
media.alt: Empowering a Generation of Confident, Caring Teachers

content.text: The Aga Khan University's Institute for Educational Development, East Africa (IED, EA) is celebrating the remarkable success and lasting impact of its Foundations for Learning (F4L) project. This three-year initiative (2022-2025) has significantly strengthened teacher education across East Africa, fundamentally enhancing teaching quality and innovation through robust professional development.

F4L was a powerful regional collaboration, training a total of 171 tutors across key teacher training institutions in Kenya, Tanzania, and Uganda. Its successful culmination in Kenya saw 53 tutors certified at Shanzu Teachers College in Mombasa. This impact was replicated regionally, reaching 29 tutors at Nachingwea Teachers College in Tanzania and 89 tutors across Lodonga and Arua Training Colleges in West Nile, Uganda. This cross-border reach reflects AKU's deep commitment to fostering sustainable, systemic change in teacher education across the region.

The F4L project's rigorous curriculum was designed to equip college tutors - the mentors of future teachers - with cutting-edge skills. The eight intensive modules focused on delivering a truly modern educational experience, emphasizing: Modern Pedagogical Practices and Inclusive Learning Environments; Integrating Gender and Diversity considerations in the classroom; and Effective use of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) in teaching.

Beyond theoretical knowledge, the project encouraged practical innovation. Tutors developed crucial mentorship and leadership skills and gained hands-on experience in Makerspace development. This creative, low- or no-cost approach to resource creation is sparking a wave of innovation that has extended beyond the colleges, with nearby schools and colleges now producing their own effective teaching aids, significantly enhancing classroom learning.

The project's alignment with national priorities was evident at the certification ceremony, which saw key education officials in attendance, including Mr Masibu Kitui, County Director of Education for Mombasa County. Mr Kitui highly commended the F4L programme for complementing national retooling efforts led by the Teachers Service Commission, underscoring the vital role of public-private partnerships in building teacher capacity and improving education outcomes.

This sentiment was reinforced by Professor Jane Rarieya, Dean at IED-EA, who reiterated the necessity of focusing on teaching quality to fully realize educational reforms: "Kenya has made substantial progress in expanding access to education through key reforms such as the CBC and the Teacher Education Framework," she said. "Yet access alone is not enough. The quality of teaching and learning remains our greatest opportunity. Your role as college tutors is pivotal the way you prepare and mentor student teachers ensures that every learner in Kenya is taught by a competent, caring, and confident teacher."

The F4L project's impact is designed to be long-lasting. Shanzu Teachers College has embraced its new role as a hub for ongoing professional development, ensuring the gains made through F4L will continue to advance AKU's mission of improving education across Kenya and the region.
